subject: CAIQ bulk evidence batch transfer and tenant-scope clarification
messages:
From: Maria Santos <maria.santos@greenfieldhealth.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@greenfieldhealth.com
Date: Wed, 7 Jan 2026 09:12:22 -0800
Subject: CAIQ export & tenant scope — audit window Jan 20

Hi Vanessa,

We kick off our CSA/CAIQ review for our annual vendor audit next month. Can Redwood provide a consolidated CAIQ control crosswalk plus the bulk evidence export for our scoped tenant (greenfield-prod) covering controls related to runtime isolation, key management, telemetry, and log retention?

Specifically we need:
- A CAIQ spreadsheet with your control mapping (which control IDs map to Redwood features/components).
- Copies of runtime log samples and an example of the ephemeral key rotation log.
- Any procedural artifacts (runbooks, owner attestations) tied to those controls.

Timeline: audit reviewers expect the bundle by 2026-01-15 to start our review before a scheduled audit on 2026-01-20.

Notes on data: we cannot accept any PII or patient PHI in raw logs. Please advise how you plan to sanitize/redact. Also flag any controls where evidence is a link-only (e.g., Doc store or live console) so we can scope acceptance.

Thanks,
Maria Santos
Senior IT Auditor
Greenfield Health

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Maria Santos <maria.santos@greenfieldhealth.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 7 Jan 2026 10:05:14 -0800
Subject: Re: CAIQ export & tenant scope — audit window Jan 20

Hi Maria — thanks for the clear ask and timeline. We can provide the CAIQ crosswalk and a packaged evidence export for greenfield-prod. High-level plan:

1) Control crosswalk (xlsx) that maps CAIQ IDs to our implementation + artifact pointers.
2) Zipped artifact bundle with: sampled runtime logs (obfuscated), key rotation proof (audit log snippet), runbooks and owner attestations.
3) Manifest indicating whether evidence is an uploaded artifact or a link-only console reference.

Owners: Jonas will lead artifact collection and upload to a secure S3 share. Priya will own log sampling and PII/PHI redaction. I will coordinate delivery and the manifest.

We will target an upload by 2026-01-12 EOD PT to give your reviewers 3 business days before 1/15. Does that work? If you require earlier, we can prioritize critical controls first.

Also: can you confirm the exact tenant name you want in the manifest (greenfield-prod vs greenfield-prod-eu) and whether you need any records to show data residency?

Vanessa Ortiz
Head, Customer Security Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Maria Santos <maria.santos@greenfieldhealth.com>
Cc: priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 8 Jan 2026 08:33:02 -0800
Subject: Re: CAIQ export & tenant scope — audit window Jan 20

Thanks Vanessa — confirming commitment. Quick notes on deliverables and technical approach:

- Files to include in the evidence bundle: redwood_caiq_crosswalk_v1.xlsx, s3_evidence_export_greenfield_20260106.zip (manifest inside), log_samples_runtime_202512-202601.txt (sampled and obfuscated), key_rotation_audit_20251231.txt, access_control_attestations.pdf, runtime_isolation_runbook_v2.md.
- Redaction approach for logs: we will hash user identifiers (sha256 truncated) and remove free-text fields that could contain PHI. We will also exclude payload bodies for any request traces. Priya will provide a short redaction summary describing the transformations.
- Residency: greenfield-prod is hosted in us-west-2. If you need eu residency evidence (greenfield-prod-eu), we need a separate scoped export.
- Delivery: artifacts uploaded to the secure S3 path and a read-only Drive folder with the crosswalk spreadsheet. We will provide a signed manifest with checksums.

Maria — action for you: confirm tenant (greenfield-prod) and approve the redaction approach so Priya can proceed with sampling.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Senior Security Engineer, Risk & Controls
Redwood Inference

From: Maria Santos <maria.santos@greenfieldhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, procurement@greenfieldhealth.com
Date: Thu, 8 Jan 2026 11:47:59 -0800
Subject: Re: CAIQ export & tenant scope — audit window Jan 20

Jonas — thanks for the breakdown. Confirmed: tenant is greenfield-prod (us-west-2). The redaction approach sounds acceptable; please ensure hashing is irreversible and include a short description in the manifest.

A couple of follow-ups:
- Our reviewers sometimes request evidence of rotation frequency (e.g., key rotation cadence). Can you include the rotation policy excerpt or a dated attestation showing the last successful rotation?
- For runtime isolation, they prefer a minimally sampled audit showing process-level isolation (container IDs, node tags) but no command-line args or environment dumps.

If you hit any blockers, please flag immediately — procurement timeline is sensitive because we need the package to finalize renewal paperwork.

Thanks,
Maria

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Maria Santos <maria.santos@greenfieldhealth.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 16:42:11 -0800
Subject: Re: CAIQ export & tenant scope — audit window Jan 20

Hi Maria / Vanessa — upload complete. Summary of what we delivered:

- redwood_caiq_crosswalk_v1.xlsx (maps CAIQ control IDs to Redwood features + artifact pointers).
- s3_evidence_export_greenfield_20260106.zip (contains sampled, obfuscated runtime logs; key rotation snippet; manifest + checksums).
- log_samples_runtime_202512-202601.txt (sampled lines with user IDs hashed; payloads removed).
- key_rotation_audit_20251231.txt (timestamped rotation event + operator id redacted).
- runtime_isolation_runbook_v2.md and access_control_attestations.pdf (owner-signed).

Location: artifacts are in the secure S3 share (s3://redwood-secure/evidence/greenfield/2026-01) and a read-only Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-greenfield-caiq

A few implementation notes included in the manifest: hashing algorithm (sha256 truncated to 12 chars), explicit list of removed fields, file-level checksums, and the contact for follow-ups (jonas_weber@redwood.com). If your reviewers need a narrower sample or live console screenshots for link-only controls, let us know and we will produce a targeted bundle.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Security Analyst
Redwood Inference
